policy_title: Pledge Not to Increase Family Home Taxes
stated: Under the Family Home Tax Guarantee, the Conservative Party pledges not to increase the number of council tax bands, undertake an expensive council tax revaluation, cut council tax discounts, or increase the rate or level of Stamp Duty, and will maintain Private Residence Relief.

source.quote: Under the Family Home Tax Guarantee, we will not increase the number of council tax bands, undertake an expensive council tax revaluation or cut council tax discounts... We will maintain Private Residence Relief so that people’s homes are protected from Capital Gains Tax and we will not increase the rate or level of Stamp Duty to support homeowners.

bearing_set.reason: Council tax levels and Stamp Duty directly affect household bills and transaction costs on home purchase, materially impacting disposable income and cost of living for ordinary households.
Stamp Duty rates and Private Residence Relief affect the cost of moving and home purchase affordability; freezing council tax bands and discounts affects the ongoing cost burden of housing tenure.

The pledge directly prevents increases in council tax rates/bands and stamp duty, preserving household take-home pay and avoiding higher transaction costs for home buyers — a real verdict on the tax burden individuals face.

Ruling out council tax revaluation and band increases forecloses potentially significant revenue options (England's bands still reflect 1991 valuations), materially constraining fiscal headroom and sustainability of the public finances.

Council tax's 1991-valuation structure is well-documented as regressive (high-value properties undertaxed relative to current worth); not revaluing preserves that distributional distortion, and maintaining Private Residence Relief continues a major CGT exemption that disproportionately benefits wealthier owner-occupiers — a real verdict on the rich-poor gap.

membership_note: The policy is primarily a tax-freeze pledge with clear, mechanistically separable effects on household tax burden (O11), fiscal headroom (O12), and distributional fairness of the tax system (O14). Stamp duty has a marginal bearing on housing transaction costs but does not materially move core housing affordability indicators (supply, rent, house-price-to-income), so O1 is excluded as below the non-negligible bar.
